name: Kelvex Transit Operator Night Shift Rig
description:
The Kelvex MagRail night shift uniform is a study in deep navy and fatigue. The anchor piece is a structured navy wool-analog duty jacket with a mandarin collar, double-breasted snap closure, and Kelvex Transit Authority insignia embroidered in silver thread on the left breast — a stylized rail line bisecting a hexagon. The right shoulder carries a removable rank tab in brushed aluminum. Underneath is a long-sleeve performance polo in the same navy, moisture-wicking and odor-resistant for twelve-hour platform duty. The jacket's rear collar panel has a low-profile port channel for BCI hardware, sealed with a magnetic cover flap when not in use. Charcoal straight-leg transit trousers with a reinforced seat and double-stitched inner thigh run clean and pressed, held by a heavy-duty webbing belt with a brushed metal buckle stamped with the KTA hex logo.

Footwear is the Kelvex MagLock Flatfoot — a low-profile composite-soled slip-resistant shoe in matte black, designed for maglev platform edges where static discharge is a real concern. A reflective piping strip runs along the shoe's outer edge. The operator wears a navy transit cap with a stiff brim and silver KTA badge, and carries a handheld scanner unit holstered at the hip in a molded synth-leather case. In cold months a charcoal-grey insulated liner vest adds warmth beneath the jacket. The uniform is pressed and regulation-correct but subtly personalized: a small enamel pin of a local shrine festival on the inside collar, invisible on shift.
functionality: BCI port channel with magnetic cover at rear collar, anti-static footwear for maglev platform safety, moisture management for extended shift wear, scanner holster, rank tab system, insulated liner option for cold weather operations
what_it_says: Stable employment with a corponation transit authority. This person has passed background checks, held a job long enough to earn a rank tab, and shows up on time. The pressed trousers and polished shoes signal someone who takes the uniform seriously — either from pride, fear of demerit points, or both. The hidden festival pin is the only thing that is theirs.
worn_by: night shift transit crew across the Circuit corridor
manufacturer: Kelvex Transit Authority — standard issue uniform, employee-maintained
price_range: Φ 220–Φ 310 (issued at no cost, replacement fines apply)
story_hooks: The operator's scanner has been logging anomalous passenger data to an off-network address for three weeks — and they have no idea, or claim not to.
A character needs to move something across three maglev lines without being scanned; the only person who can help is someone in this uniform who owes a favor.
The rank tab on the shoulder belongs to a grade the wearer has not yet earned — and someone in KTA Internal Compliance has noticed.
related_entities: Ringo Heavy Transit MagRail Levitation Transport Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharp, militaristic silhouette with authoritative presence. The navy duty jacket commands attention with its structured lines and mandarin collar, projecting operational competence and institutional hierarchy. Worn by someone who moves between platforms and machinery with practiced efficiency.
physical_description.fit: Tailored but not restrictive—designed for twelve-hour mobility. The jacket sits square on the shoulders with enough room for layering. Trousers are straight-leg and pressed, creating clean vertical lines. The overall cut is regulation-formal, not fashion-forward.
physical_description.primary_material: Navy wool-analog synthetic for the jacket and cap; performance-blend poly for the moisture-wicking polo; heavyweight cotton-weave for the charcoal trousers; matte composite with synth-leather accents for the shoe and scanner holster.
physical_description.texture: The jacket has a slight nap, catching light subtly. The polo is smooth and engineered for durability. Trousers are crisp with tight weave. The MagLock shoe sole is slightly textured for grip. The brushed aluminum rank tab and belt buckle are intentionally matte to reduce glare on night shifts.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep navy as primary (jacket, polo, cap); charcoal grey (trousers, liner vest, shoe); silver accents (embroidered insignia, rank tab, badge, belt buckle); black reflective piping on shoe outer edge; white or cream internal collar lining visible at mandarin collar edges.
physical_description.closures: Double-breasted magnetic snap closure on jacket (reliable in electromagnetic environments); standard button placket on polo; webbing belt with brushed metal KTA-stamped buckle; slip-on MagLock shoe design with low-profile lace alternatives; magnetic cover flap over rear neck BCI port.
distinctive_features: Embroidered KTA insignia on left breast: stylized rail line bisecting a hexagon in silver thread
Low-profile BCI hardware port channel in rear collar with magnetic security flap
Removable brushed aluminum rank tab on right shoulder
Reinforced seat and double-stitched inner thigh on trousers (platform duty wear)
Reflective piping strip on shoe outer edge for maglev platform visibility
Molded synth-leather hip holster for handheld scanner unit
Optional charcoal-grey insulated liner vest for cold months
Stiff-brimmed transit cap with silver KTA badge
Static-discharge rated MagLock Flatfoot sole design
Hidden interior collar pin: local shrine festival enamel (personal customization)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional—working-class infrastructure employee. The uniform signals stable employment with a major metropolitan authority. Not luxury, but quality and purpose-built. Worn by those who maintain the systems others rely on.
physical_description.cultural_context: Transit infrastructure operator. Someone disciplined by schedules, machinery logic, and public safety protocols. Likely mixed heritage reflective of GLMZ demographics (the hidden shrine pin suggests East/Southeast Asian cultural identity). The BCI port indicates this worker is augmented for duty efficiency. Wearing this means you are essential infrastructure.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pressed and regulation-correct during shifts, but subtly worn in character. The jacket shows creases from repeated movement. The trousers are clean but the inner thigh shows patina from daily wear. The shoe sole has minor scuff marks from platform edges. The uniform is maintained but not pristine—it's a working uniform, not dress uniform. Personal items (the shrine pin) indicate long-term ownership and identity investment.
